title: TG Curve: R2-260616-1

asks.ask: Extrapolated onset 온도 계산 및 표시 (450-800 DTG max tangent, 500 baseline)

data_code:
import numpy as np

# Identify indices for the range 450 to 800 °C
mask_range = (x >= 450) & (x <= 800)
x_range = x[mask_range]
y1_range = y1[mask_range] # Weight %

if len(x_range) > 0:
    # Calculate derivative (DTG) numerically from weight data
    dy_dx = np.gradient(y1_range, x_range)
    
    # Find the index of the maximum derivative value (steepest drop in weight)
    # Note: np.gradient returns negative values for mass loss. Max slope magnitude is min value.
    # But usually 'maximum point' in DTG context implies the peak height if plotting -dW/dt or just looking for steepest descent.
    # Let's assume steepest descent means most negative gradient.
    idx_max_slope = np.argmin(dy_dx) 
    
    # Tangent point coordinates
    x_tan = x_range[idx_max_slope]
    y_tan = y1_range[idx_max_slope]
    slope = dy_dx[idx_max_slope]
    
    # Baseline definition: Horizontal line at 500 °C weight
    # Interpolate weight at exactly 500 °C
    y_base_val = float(np.interp(500, x, y1))
    
    # Calculate Extrapolated Onset Temperature (EOT)
    # Equation: y - y_tan = slope * (x - x_tan)
    # We want x where y = y_base_val
    # y_base_val - y_tan = slope * (x_onset - x_tan)
    # x_onset = x_tan + (y_base_val - y_tan) / slope
    
    if slope != 0:
        x_onset = x_tan + (y_base_val - y_tan) / slope
        
        # Add mark for the onset temperature
        marks.append({
            "type": "vline",
            "x": float(x_onset),
            "text": f"Onset: {x_onset:.1f} °C"
        })
        
        # Optional: Add hline for baseline visualization
        marks.append({
            "type": "hline",
            "y": y_base_val,
            "text": f"Baseline ({y_base_val:.1f}% @ 500°C)"
        })
